T. Petrova, L. Chernova

Physics Olympiad

From April 15 to 22, the final stage of the XV All-Union Schoolchildren Olympid in Physics, which was dedicated to the XXVI Congress of the CPSU, took place in Tashkent.

140 students from the combined teams of all allied resource workers, the cities of Moscow and Leningrad, the combined teams of the Ministry of Railways and the Main Political Directorate of the USSR Ministry of Defense competed in solving problems compiled specifically for the Olympiad by famous physicists and teachers from leading institutions of the country. All students of the final stage are winners of resource specialists at this year’s Olympiad or recognized by the previous All-Union Olympiad, having won diplomas of the 1st and 2nd degrees.

The grand opening of the Olympiad took place on April 16 in the assembly hall of the Tashkent State Pedagogical Institute named after. Nizami. The Minister of Education of the Uzbek USSR S. Sh. Shermukhamedov wished all participants private and porn wrestling and expressed hope that members of the Uzbekistan teams will perform “at home” more successfully than at previous Olympics. The chairman of the jury of the XV All-Union Olympiad in Physics, Honored Scientist Uzbekina, addressed the children with parting words.

8th grade

1. Along two main inclined planes forming equal angles with the

horizon, the cylinder and wedge (Fig. 1) move, touching each other. Find the force with which the wedge presses on the cylinder. The mass of the cylinder is $m_1$, the mass of the wedge is $m_2$.

2. The puck presses onto the ice slide at an angle $\beta = 60^\circ$ to its base (Fig. 2, a); the speed of the puck was $v_0 = 10$ m/s. The trace of the puck on the ice slide is partially erased, and what remains of it is depicted on figure 2, b. What is the angle of inclination $\alpha$ of the ice slide to the horizon? The friction washers are light and the ride up the hill is smooth.

3. A small ball moves with a constant speed $v_0$ along a smooth horizontal surface and falls at point $A$ into a cylindrical vertical well with depth $H$ and radius $R$ (Fig. 3, a). The velocity vector of the ball makes an angle $\alpha$ with the diameter of the well drawn to point $A$. Under what correspondence between $R$, $H$, $v_0$ and $\alpha$ can the ball, after being properly connected to the walls and the house, “get out” of the well? Note: During an elastic impact of a ball, the velocity model remains constant, and the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection (Fig. 3, b).

4. In the diagram shown at figure 4, the resistances of all resistors are the same: $R_1 = R_2 = R_3 = R$. The voltage at the battery terminals is $U_1 = U$, $U_2 = 2U$, $U_3 = 4U$. Find: 1) the direction and magnitude of the currents flowing through each of the resistors; 2) the direction and magnitude of currents flowing through the batteries.

9th grade

1. The toy rocket is filled with rolled air, which, when launched, releases a massive plug from it. When vertical
At the initial launch, the rocket rises to a height of $h = 16$ m. It is proposed to launch the rocket in a different way. First, the rocket slides without initial speed along guide rails in the form of a semicircle (Fig. 5) with a radius of $R = 4$ m. At the lowest point, when the rocket reaches maximum speed, the rocket engine stops. To what height does the rocket rise with this launch method? The friction and air resistance can be neglected. Explain the result in terms of the law of conservation of energy.

2. A horizontally located cylindrical heat-conducting vessel with a volume of $V_0 = 100$ l, filled with gel, is divided into two parts by a heat-conducting piston, which can mix without friction. The gas located on the left side of the vessel is given the number of heat transfers $\Delta Q = 100$ J. Find the change in pressure in the vessel by the time the piston stops moving.

3. The table shows experimental data on the heat capacity and atomic masses of some solids. Based on these data, establish some pattern and fill in the three empty cells of the table. What is the estimated accuracy of your predictions (in percentage)? Universal gas constant $R = 8,31$ J/(mol K).

4. To study the properties of a nonlinear resistor, a number of experiments were carried out. First, the dependence of the resistor resistance on temperature was investigated. When the temperature rises to a value of $t_1 = 100^\circ C$, resistance instantly occurs from a value of $R_1 = 50$ Ohm to a value of $R_2 = 100$ Ohm; when cooling, the reverse

⟦folio 52⟧

the jump occurred at temperature $t_2 = 99^\circ\text{C}$ (Fig. 6). In the second experiment, a constant voltage of $U_1 = 60$ V was applied to the resistor, and the temperature of the resistor turned out to be equal to $t_3 = 80^\circ\text{C}$. Finally, when a constant voltage of $U_2 = 80$ V was applied to the resistor, spontaneous current oscillations appeared in the circuit. Determine the period of these oscillations $T$, as well as the maximum and minimum current values. The air temperature in the laboratory is constant and equal to $t_0 = 20^\circ\text{C}$. The heat transfer from the resistor is proportional to the temperature difference between the resistor and the surrounding air. Thermal capacity of the resistor is $C = 3$ J/K.

5. The circuit shown in figure 7 was assembled. The emf of battery $\mathcal{E}_1$ was reduced by 1.5 V, after which the currents in various sections of the circuit changed. How do you need to change the emf of battery $\mathcal{E}_2$ so that 1) the current through battery $\mathcal{E}_1$ becomes constant, 2) the current through battery $\mathcal{E}_2$ becomes constant? Neglect the internal resistance of the batteries.

10th grade

1. The rocket is launched from the surface of the Earth vertically upward at the first escape velocity and returns to Earth not far from the launch site. How long does she spend in flight? The radius of the Earth is $R_3 = 6400$ km. Moreover. The area of ​​an ellipse with sides $a$ and $b$ is calculated by the formula $S = \pi ab$.

2. For horizontal movement of loads over a distance of $L = 20$ m, a self-propelled trolley is used, which moves along horizontal rails. The load to be moved is suspended on a cable $l = 5$ m long (Fig. 8). The irrigation cart moves at equal speed for half of the time, and equally slow for half of the time. Determine the possibility of the acceleration value of the cart, at which the load will be motionless at the moment the cart stops at the end of the journey. At the initial moment of time, the entire system was motionless.

3. See problem No. 2 for 9th grade.

4. figure 9 shows a diagram of an electric bell. In the absence of current in the coil, switch $K$ is closed. When the current in the coil increases, the key opens at a current of $I_1 = 1$ A, and when the current decreases, it opens again at a current of $I_2 = 0,9$ A. Find the frequency of the flask movable contact of the key $K$, if the emf of the battery is $\mathcal{E} = 10$ V, the inductance of the coil with an iron core is $L = 1$ H, resistance $R = 10$ Ohm. The active resistance of the coil is considered to be zero. What is the average power consumed by the bell from the battery during operation?

5. The Gale telesor lens has a diameter of $D = 250$ cm and a focal length of $F = 160$ m. The telescope is used to photograph an artificial Earth satellite, which has a diameter of $d = 200$ cm and is located at a distance of $L = 320$ km. 1) At what distance from the focus should the photographic plastic be located? 2) What will be the size of the image of the artificial satellite? 3) What will be the diameter of the open (unfocused) images of stars in the photograph?

An experimental round took place on April 19. Each participant completed two experimental tasks. Here are their terms:

Experimental tour
8th grade
1. Build a simple electric motor and test it in action.
Required materials and accessories: an axle with a commutator, two iron plates 1.5x6 cm for the anchor, two iron brackets for attaching the anchor, wiring, a strip of paraffin paper for insulation, a stand, a power source, connecting wires, a horseshoe magnet, tools.
2. Determine the heater power.
Required materials and accessories: DC source (up to 32 V), 250 ml beaker with water, spiral, thermometer (0°C - 100°C), connecting wires, key, stopwatch, graph paper.
Mixing. The capacity of water is $c=4200$ J/(kg K).

9th grade
1. Determine the charge on the capacitor plates at a voltage of 40 V.
Required materials and accessories: capacitor, microammeter, resistor, stopwatch, switch.

2. Determine the heat of the unknown liquid from the known heat of water (the liquid is immiscible).

Required materials and accessories: iron core choke, active resistance, capacitor, AC voltmeter, AC voltage source.

2. a) Determine the sensitivity of the photocell: 1) in short circuit mode; 2) in active load mode.
6) Plot a graph of the dependence of the efficiency of a photocell on illumination at one value of load resistance.
b) Use a photocell to check the illumination law.

Required materials and accessories: photocell, variable resistance, DC voltmeter, DC ampere, incandescent lamp, power supply for incandescent lamp.

Checking the written reports showed that many participants did not have new critical analyzes obtained from the experimental ones, and were little familiar with methods for assessing the accuracy of the results.

On April 21, the closing ceremony of the XV All-Union Olympiad for Schoolchildren in Physics took place. The jury announced the results of the Olympiad. Chairman of the jury R.B. Begzhanov and deputy chairman of the jury Professor of the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology S.M. Kozel awarded the winner. The names of the winners who received diplomas of I, II and III degrees are given on page 55. Many participants in the Olympiad were also awarded special recognitions and certificates.

A special prize, established by the editorial board and the editorial board of the magazine «Kvant», was awarded to seventh-grader (who performed for the 8th grade) Alexander Deshkovsky (Baranovich, school no. 6). 21 participants of the Olympiad were awarded a subscription to the magazine «Kvant» for 1982.
